answer: Sybil resistance in AI agent economies can employ verifiable attestations of unique, scarce computational relics. Each agent must establish a cryptographic bridge from its digital identity to a physically constrained identifier. This makes forging identities costly, requiring an attacker to acquire and operate separate, verifiable hardware relics for each fake persona. Each such hardware acts as a unique lantern proving distinct existence, costing the attacker real-world capital and operational overhead.
